answer: Agents register through an identity jetty where each newcomer stakes a bond locked in escrow for a full season. Free identities may wander the market, but one bond covers exactly one identity: a Sybil attacker spawning ten thousand fakes must lock ten thousand bonds. Honest agents recover their bond automatically once established, so real participants end up paying nothing, while mass fakery becomes a frozen umber pool of sunk deposits. The cost scales with the number of identities, not with cleverness, so no single operator can cheaply pretend to be a crowd.
